audience: Students with basic programming knowledge learning assembly

progression.localImplementation: Native prose, public intermediate and final CLI checks; remote lesson runner and enforced policies remain pending

title: Multiply matrices in clipped tiles
prerequisites: Exact signed products and full-width sums
Function frames and logical memory intervals
learningObjectives: Handle empty output and zero reduction separately
Retain partial sums across clipped reduction tiles
Compare instruction work, data notices and cache placement
Accept equivalent correct schedules under one interface

steps.title: Trace a rectangular product before writing loops

quiz.prompt: Which values determine output row one, column zero?

choices.text: The second left row and first right column.
The second row of both inputs.
Only the diagonal of each input.

hints.text: Fix one output row and column before following k.
For C[1,0], pair 4,5,6 with 7,9,11.

steps.title: Separate row stride from tile edge

quiz.prompt: What determines the right-input reduction stride?

hints.text: Keep the original packed row widths beside each address formula.
A tile edge limits iteration; it does not become the stride of B.

steps.title: Prove the width of a partial sum

quiz.prompt: Which part must retain more than thirty-two bits?

hints.text: Calculate two minimum-times-minimum products explicitly.
The sum crosses the signed-word endpoint before the individual product does.

steps.title: Inspect the supplied frame and safe exits

quiz.prompt: When should the saved registers be restored?

choices.text: After releasing the stack frame and overwriting its contents.
Before releasing their private stack storage.

hints.text: Locate the saved slots and the restoring exit before replacing a region.
The provisional branch uses that exit so unfinished code still obeys register preservation.

steps.title: Guard empty scalar output and start row zero

quiz.prompt: Which shape needs no output store?

hints.text: Ask whether any output row and column both exist.
Test M and N before entering a body that can load or store a matrix element.

steps.title: Reset the scalar column at each row

quiz.prompt: Where must column zero be established?

choices.text: At the start of every output row.

hints.text: Separate entering a new row from entering a new cell.
The row label must reset j; the column loop must leave that reset behind.

steps.title: Start a fresh reduction for each output cell

quiz.prompt: Why clear the sum inside the column loop?

choices.text: Every output cell has its own dot product.
The previous sum is always an input operand.

hints.text: Write the invariant for zero products consumed.
Both the reduction index and the accumulator start at zero for every output.

steps.title: Form the full left-row address

quiz.prompt: Which factor converts a left-input element offset into bytes?

hints.text: Count elements before row i before converting to bytes.
Use i*K words, scale by four, then add the full left base.

steps.title: Form the right-column address and row stride

quiz.prompt: What stays fixed as the right walker advances?

hints.text: Follow one fixed column across the physical rows of B.
The first position is column j; successive positions differ by N stored words.

steps.title: Skip the scalar reduction when K is zero

quiz.prompt: What is the output of a nonempty zero-reduction product?

hints.text: An empty sum has a value even when no input pair exists.
Bypass the pair loads for K=0 and continue toward the output store with a zero accumulator.

steps.title: Load one signed left value

quiz.prompt: How should stored -32768 be interpreted?

hints.text: The value is stored in a word even though its numerical range is narrower.
Use a signed word load; the register must retain a negative input as a negative full-width value.

steps.title: Load the matching signed right value

quiz.prompt: Which pair belongs to reduction position zero?

choices.text: A[0,0] and B[0,0] for the first output.

hints.text: Match the same reduction position in both inputs.
Keep the left operand in `t7` while loading the right operand through its separate walker.

steps.title: Compute the exact signed product

quiz.prompt: Can the loaded left operand be replaced by its product here?

choices.text: No; it is the immutable source memory.
Yes; the register value has already been consumed.
Only if the product is zero.

hints.text: Distinguish the loaded operand from the memory it came from.
After forming the product, the left-operand register can hold that product; the input memory remains unchanged.

steps.title: Add the product to the full scalar sum

quiz.prompt: What does the sum contain immediately after this edit?

hints.text: Track how many products the sum represents before incrementing k.
Add the full product into `t3` with a doubleword addition.

steps.title: Consume the row and column until K products are complete

quiz.prompt: When is the scalar sum complete?

hints.text: Each iteration consumes one row value and one column value.
Advance A by one word, B by one full right row, and repeat until k reaches K.

steps.title: Address the current doubleword output

quiz.prompt: Why shift the output offset by three?

choices.text: The input words have eight bytes.

hints.text: Output cells are twice as wide as input words.
Use i*N+j as the element index and scale it by eight before adding C.

steps.title: Store both halves of the completed output

quiz.prompt: What must an output store preserve?

choices.text: All eight bytes of the exact result.

hints.text: Inspect the high word of the two-product boundary result.
A full result needs a doubleword store even when the default small example fits a word.

steps.title: Advance the scalar column and restart its reduction

quiz.prompt: Which state must restart for the next output column?

choices.text: The reduction index, accumulator and input walkers.

hints.text: A new column starts a new dot product.
Branch to the column initialization so its sum and both walkers restart.

steps.title: Advance the scalar row and complete the baseline

quiz.prompt: Why target `naive_row` after changing the row?

choices.text: It resets the column for the new row.
It restores every output to sentinel.
It repeats the previous row address.

hints.text: The old row has already consumed all columns.
Return to the row label so the next row begins again at column zero.

steps.title: Select the tiled function without changing the contract

quiz.prompt: What changes when the selector becomes one?

choices.text: The word width of both inputs.
The right matrix is automatically transposed.

hints.text: Keep the source used for preparing recipes at its documented defaults.
The recipe writes method one into a separate observation file for the tiled entry.

steps.title: Guard empty tiled output

quiz.prompt: May an empty output call clear the first product cell?

choices.text: No; there is no selected output cell.
Yes; mapped memory is always writable.

hints.text: Consider an output interval of length zero.
Place both output-dimension tests before the first zeroing store.

steps.title: Count the product cells to initialize

quiz.prompt: What unit does the zeroing counter use?

hints.text: Keep the units of the counter and pointer separate.
Count M*N cells while the pointer moves eight bytes for each cell.

steps.title: Initialize one full output cell

quiz.prompt: Why initialize before reading a partial sum?

choices.text: A previous call always produced the same answer.
The caller grants arbitrary initial output contents.

hints.text: A partial-sum load will later read all eight bytes.
Initialize the entire doubleword without reading its old contents.

steps.title: Initialize the complete product interval

quiz.prompt: Which bytes may this loop clear?

hints.text: The zeroing body handles one complete cell per visit.
Advance by eight and subtract one cell; the empty-output guard handles the zero-iteration case.

steps.title: Return a zero reduction or start the first row tile

quiz.prompt: When does a zero-reduction product become complete?

choices.text: After every selected output cell is zeroed.
After loading one input from each matrix.

hints.text: The zeroing work already gives the answer for an empty reduction.
Return after zeroing when K=0; otherwise establish the first row-tile start.

steps.title: Clip the row-tile exclusive end

quiz.prompt: Which row index is excluded from this tile?

hints.text: Write the half-open row interval before coding the comparison.
Choose the smaller of I+T and M without changing the stored start I.

steps.title: Reset the column-tile start for each row band

quiz.prompt: Why is using `fp` here compatible with the interface?

choices.text: Its incoming full value is saved and restored.
It is always zero on entry.

hints.text: Every new row band needs all of the output columns.
Reset J to zero after calculating the row end, before entering its first column tile.

steps.title: Clip the column-tile exclusive end

quiz.prompt: Which dimension clips the column end?

hints.text: The right and output matrices share a column count.
Clip J+T against N, keeping element width out of the index comparison.

steps.title: Restart the reduction tiles for this output tile

quiz.prompt: When should the reduction-tile start return to zero?

choices.text: At the start of each output tile.

hints.text: A different output tile has not yet received any dot-product segments.
Restart L at zero for every new output tile.

steps.title: Clip the reduction-tile exclusive end

quiz.prompt: What bounds the last reduction pair?

choices.text: The size of the mapped data segment.

hints.text: Consider K smaller than T and K not divisible by T.
Clip L+T against K so the segment stops at the final real pair.

steps.title: Start the current output row at I

quiz.prompt: Which start initializes the current output row?

hints.text: The outer tile start and inner current row are distinct state.
Copy I into i at the beginning of each reduction tile.

steps.title: Start the current output column at J

quiz.prompt: Why reset j for every row?

choices.text: The previous row consumed its selected columns.
The right matrix has become transposed.

hints.text: Each row in a tile needs its whole selected column interval.
Copy J into j whenever the row loop starts a new row.

steps.title: Address the current output partial sum

quiz.prompt: Which index expression identifies this cell?

hints.text: Keep this output address available through the complete segment.
Form i*N+j and scale by eight; retain the result in the dedicated C walker.

steps.title: Reload the initialized partial sum

quiz.prompt: What belongs in the accumulator before a later reduction tile?

choices.text: The already accumulated output partial sum.

hints.text: Think about what the second reduction tile must preserve.
Load the previously stored full sum, which is zero only on the first segment.

steps.title: Address the left input at the reduction-tile start

quiz.prompt: Which reduction index belongs in this start address?

hints.text: The segment begins at L rather than reduction position zero.
Address A[i,L] using the physical left row width K.

steps.title: Address the right input at the same reduction start

quiz.prompt: Why use N in L*N+j?

choices.text: A tile has repacked the right input.
N is the actual right-input row width.

hints.text: Use the same L in the two input starts.
Address B[L,j] with row width N; T has not changed the representation.

steps.title: Retain the right stride and current reduction index

quiz.prompt: Why can `a3` hold a stride now?

choices.text: The descriptor fields are already retained elsewhere.
Arguments are never needed by a function.

hints.text: The original descriptor pointer is no longer needed after its fields are retained.
Reuse its argument register for 4N and initialize k from L.

steps.title: Load the matched pair inside this tile

quiz.prompt: What does `t4` represent before these operands are added?

hints.text: Leave the existing accumulator untouched while fetching operands.
Load a signed word from each walker at the same reduction position.

steps.title: Form a full product for the tiled sum

quiz.prompt: Does changing tile edge alter the product arithmetic?

choices.text: Yes; a larger tile requires rounding.
No; the same signed values are multiplied.

hints.text: Blocking changes traversal, while the arithmetic domain remains fixed.
Multiply the signed operands into a full product before adding it to the retained sum.

steps.title: Extend the retained output sum

quiz.prompt: When does this new private sum become visible in C?

choices.text: When the tile bound is calculated.

hints.text: At a later segment, the accumulator already includes previous contributions.
Extend `t4` with the current product; do not replace `t4` with the product.

steps.title: Consume exactly the clipped reduction segment

quiz.prompt: What does `a2` hold in this loop?

hints.text: The endpoint is an original reduction index, not a segment length.
Start k at L and stop at the clipped end after advancing both physical walkers.

steps.title: Publish this segment contribution

quiz.prompt: Is this segment store always the final output value?

choices.text: Only if it is the last reduction segment for that cell.
Yes; a tile contains the entire matrix.
No; no partial sum may ever be stored.

hints.text: The public output can temporarily hold an incomplete dot product.
Store the full segment sum through the C pointer retained before the input walks.

steps.title: Visit every selected column in the current row

quiz.prompt: Which state must remain independent between neighboring cells?

hints.text: Neighboring cells have independent partial sums.
Restart the cell body for each j until the clipped column endpoint.

steps.title: Visit every selected row in this output tile

quiz.prompt: What does the next reduction tile need from this state?

choices.text: The stored partial sum of each output cell.

hints.text: The next row must begin at J again.
Advance i and branch to the row label, which resets the current column.

steps.title: Advance L and retain earlier tile contributions

quiz.prompt: What would resetting the partial sum at this stage discard?

hints.text: The next group contributes to the same output cells.
Advance L by T, reclip its end, and reload every stored partial sum.

steps.title: Advance J and restart its full reduction

quiz.prompt: Why restart L after advancing J?

choices.text: A new column tile contains no output elements.
The next output tile also needs every reduction position.
The input rows have been repacked.

hints.text: A new output tile needs the reduction from its beginning.
Advance J by T and target the column-tile label so L resets to zero.

steps.title: Advance I and finish all output tiles

quiz.prompt: Which bound clips the final row band?

hints.text: A new row band must revisit all column tiles.
Advance I by T and target the row-tile label so the row end and J are rebuilt.

steps.title: Observe the first reduction tile before the second

quiz.prompt: Which observation proves that the second tile must retain prior state?

choices.text: The descriptor tile edge is positive.
C already contains valid first-segment contributions.

hints.text: The first breakpoint visit occurs before any reduction segment.
Step beyond the first visit, then stop again with L=2 to inspect the first stored contributions.

steps.title: Compare complete-call instructions and cache notices

quiz.prompt: What has this measurement established?

choices.text: A tradeoff between simulated instruction work and cache-model misses.
A host elapsed-time speedup of the same ratio.
That all tile sizes have identical data traffic.

hints.text: Use the same entry and return boundaries for both functions.
Record simulated instructions, data notices and cache misses as separate columns.

steps.title: Test equivalence and a fresh second call

quiz.prompt: May free-writing grading require the illustrated temporary register assignment?

choices.text: Yes; register spelling defines the product.
No; final checks use the public arithmetic and ownership contract.
Only when the result is positive.

hints.text: Ask which internal details are observable in the public interface.
Use a second call in the same session to expose stale sums or loop state.
